title: One and Many
introduction: Practise one and many with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: Singular words name one thing. Plural words name more than one.
rules: Add -s to many nouns. Add -es to many nouns ending in s, sh, ch or x.
Some plurals change their spelling, such as baby → babies and child → children.
Use a singular noun for one and a plural noun for more than one.
Many plural nouns end in s: book, books.
Some end in es: box, boxes.

grammar.description: bus → buses; dish → dishes; box → boxes
child → children; foot → feet; tooth → teeth; person → people

exercises.question: Two ___ (dog).
exercises.solution: Add -s to dog for more than one.

exercises.question: Four ___ (cup).
exercises.solution: Add -s to cup for more than one.

exercises.question: Three ___ (bus).
exercises.solution: Add -es to nouns ending in s.

exercises.question: Five ___ (dish).
exercises.solution: Add -es to nouns ending in sh.

exercises.question: Two ___ (box).
exercises.solution: Add -es to nouns ending in x.

exercises.question: Three ___ (baby).
exercises.solution: After a consonant, change final y to ies.

exercises.question: Two ___ (toy).
exercises.solution: After a vowel, keep y and add s.

exercises.question: Two ___ (child).
exercises.solution: Child has an irregular plural form.

exercises.question: Two ___ (foot).
exercises.solution: Foot has an irregular plural: change oo to ee.

exercises.question: Three ___ (tooth).
exercises.solution: Tooth has an irregular plural: change oo to ee.

exercises.question: One ___ (chairs).
exercises.solution: One requires the singular form; remove the final s.

exercises.question: Four ___ (person).
exercises.solution: Person has an irregular plural form.

summary: Singular words name one thing. Plural words name more than one.
